My side gig went through this with SARS. Unless you're the prepper group's medic, typical PPE and disinfectant procedures are sufficient to protect you. Bacteria need four things to gain a foot-hold in your body: A bacteria, enough of the damn thing, a transmission mechanism, and your own susceptibility (broken skin, natural weaknesses such as mouth and eyes). Removal of just one of those will prevent an infection.

Bleach/water mix to disinfect your own skin and items that got touched, N95 masks, clear face shields, latex gloves, disposable booties, even disposable body suits will be sufficient to protect you. Don't kneel in blood, wash your hands, wear your glasses and facemask, wear your gloves.

If you're the medic, you'll need to create a disconnected structure from the rest of your redoubt. Coat the walls and floor with 6 mil+ plastic and tape the seams with Tuck. Install a fan to suck the air and contaminated vapours out. You'll need a something like a P100 filter mask plus all the PPE above. Double glove with disinfectant in between and tape the gloves and booties to your suit. Provide a sanitizing area outside the patient area with a bleach/water shower. Dispose of the water far away from everyone and everything, a covered rock pit is an idea. Bag and burn all your PPE every time. An assistant with their own PPE to help you disinfect and suit-up really is required. Nothing leaves the containment area. Disinfect all tools and medical gear at regular intervals (daily) and swab and disinfect the floor twice a day with bleach water. Bodies should be burned as much as possible downwind and the remains buried at 6ft or better. Isolate your medical team, if possible, from the main group for the incubation period of the plague.

If you need big respirators and bio-hazard suits, you have bigger problems, and should get the hell out while you still can.
